policy_evidence.text: Reinsurance serves as a critical risk transfer mechanism for SecureLife, allowing the company to protect itself from significant losses and stabilize financial performance. By transferring risk to reinsurers, SecureLife can manage its risk exposure more effectively, enhance capital efficiency, and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements. The objectives of the reinsurance program include optimizing the company's risk-retention balance, maintaining financial stability, and supporting business growth. With a diverse portfolio of over 500,000 policies and a target to increase premium income by 20% annually, a well-structured reinsurance program enhances SecureLife's resilience to adverse events and contributes to long-term financial sustainability.

Each General Insurance company has to prepare its annual re-insurance
program or plan (for both inward and outward reinsurance) in which it

additional_regulatory_context.text:
Audit as a control mechanism
Control mechanisms imposed on insurance companies in line with the Solvency II Directive:
• requirements relating to competences and reputations of individuals who actually manage
an insurer or occupy other key positions – Article 42,
• risk management – Articles 44 and 45,
• internal control – Article 46,
• internal audit – Article 47.
According to Article 41 of the Solvency II Directive, the selection of control mechanisms should
comply with the following principles:
• the system should have an appropriately transparent structure including clearly assigned and
divided tasks that provides for the appropriate flow of information,
• they should be subject to regular internal reviews every year as a minimum,
• they should be approved by an administrative, management or supervisory authority,
• a control system should be verified by a supervisory authority with regard to risks identified
by the insurer that may affect adequate financial standing,

Auditing, an expert auditor examining accounts can take advantage of the findings of an internal
audit and internal control with regard to the reliability and conformity of information contained in ac-
counts with applicable accounting principles (policies), provided they have previously verified that
these findings could be relied on. The need to verify the reliability of an internal audit methodology
is an added incentive to develop principles of cooperation between internal and external audits, as it
would facilitate the preparation of some joint solutions. The compulsory change of expert auditors and
the consequent need to re-establish rules of cooperation appears to pose some problems. The prob-
lem is only theoretical, though, and should be treated as an additional control mechanism helping

plied accounting principles (policies), together with the reliability and clarity of the standing

Thus, the scope of internal audits is significantly broader than that of external audits. It can-
not be said, however, that the scope of external audits is within the scope of internal audits –
in theory, accounting and finance issues, as well as financial audits are parts of internal audits,
however in this case they are usually not subject to, for example, a thorough annual review since
they are treated as lower-risk and can be excluded from internal audit schedules as a result. There-
fore, the role of external auditing does not diminish when internal audit is introduced. Verification
of an insurer’s accounts and accounting policies is the sole responsibility of expert auditors, that
is, external audits.

Insurance Review 4/2013 / Wiadomości Ubezpieczeniowe 4/2013
Conclusions
Auditing is undoubtedly a very important control mechanism for insurance companies as it supports
management processes, in particular, in the areas of finance, accounting and risk management.
Applicable legislation binds insurers not only to have their accounting policies and accounts
verified by expert auditors (external – financial auditing), but also to implement internal auditing
and audit committees, the elements of public supervision.
The introduction of these control mechanisms in pursuit of similar objectives – supporting risk
management processes in insurance companies – enforces the development of principles and ar-
eas of cooperation in order to enhance their effectiveness, reduce labour expenditures on auditing
efforts, and improve the management of risk associated with the operations of insurance companies.
The research indicates that insurers have pointed to such areas and overall principles of col-

of an insurer’s accounts and accounting policies is the sole responsibility of expert auditors, that
is, external audits.
Mutual cooperation between both types of auditing is highly recommended, not only because
the scopes of both overlap, but also due to the fact that it can be of advantage to both internal
auditors and expert auditors.
Collaboration between internal and external audits is rooted in standards governing both con-

The OECD defines corporate governance as “a set of relationships between a
company’s management, its board, its shareholders, and other stakeholders.
Corporate governance also provides the structure through which the objectives of the
company are set, and the means of attaining these objectives and monitoring
performance are determined, good corporate governance should provide proper
incentives for the board and management to pursue objectives that are in the interests
of the company and shareholders and should facilitate effective monitoring, thereby

Learning objective: To be able to review outsourcing needs.
11.1 Insurance aspects
One important factor with outsourcing, is that while it may be possible to outsource a number of activities, the
regulatory requirements cannot usually be delegated, and the insurance company remains liable to the regulatory
authority for performance.
Outsourcing has had mixed reviews and there are examples where it can work well – for example outsourcing
medical claims to providers with a good track record, and other examples where lack of a proven track record and
total underestimation of the work involved has led to disaster.
Certain Lloyd’s syndicates have outsourced motor claims successfully – a typical situation whereby smaller or-
ganisations can group their needs together and reach economies of scale and a much better result for the insured.

policy_evidence.text: Diversification: The reinsurance portfolio is diversified across multiple reinsurers to reduce counterparty risk and enhance the stability of the reinsurance program. SecureLife aims to distribute risk across at least five major reinsurers to ensure optimal risk transfer.

policy_evidence.text: Reinsurance serves as a critical risk transfer mechanism for SecureLife, allowing the company to protect itself from significant losses and stabilize financial performance. By transferring risk to reinsurers, SecureLife can manage its risk exposure more effectively, enhance capital efficiency, and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements. The objectives of the reinsurance program include optimizing the company's risk-retention balance, maintaining financial stability, and supporting business growth. With a diverse portfolio of over 500,000 policies and a target to increase premium income by 20% annually, a well-structured reinsurance program enhances SecureLife's resilience to adverse events and contributes to long-term financial sustainability.

Internal and external audits are control mechanisms tasked with the evaluation of certain processes

The principal role of the internal auditing is to support business operations by evaluating pro-
cesses of risk management and internal control. The research demonstrated that the expectations
of internal auditing chiefly involve:
• risk management,
• responding to changing business factors,
• assessment of management systems and prevailing practices.
Insurers pointed to the following key areas to be monitored by internal audits:
• business goals – support for their implementation,
• business productivity,
• staff qualifications and skills – better utilisation,
• consultancy on programmes implementing changes,
• indication of change areas,
• reducing the risk of fraud,
• consultancy on launching new products and entering new markets,
• comparison with other insurers or other similar businesses,
• continuation of business monitoring.

3.1 RISK IDENTIFICATION AND MEASUREMENT
3.1.1 An insurer should assess its activities and processes for any
vulnerability to fraud and determine the consequential impact of any potential
fraud. In determining the potential sources of fraud risk, the insurer should
consider the following:
• adequacy of measures to verify customer information before
accepting a customer’s proposal taking into consideration the
risk factors posed by different distribution channels such as
internet policy application without face-to-face contact; and
• fit and proper standards for its intermediaries.
3.1.2 The insurer should also recognise that certain products or lines of
business may be more susceptible to particular types of fraud. For instance,
for workman compensation insurance, employers may misrepresent their

business may be more susceptible to particular types of fraud. For instance,
for workman compensation insurance, employers may misrepresent their
employees’ payroll and job scope in order to pay lower premiums. Similarly,
motor insurance is susceptible to inflated claims as well as staging of
accidents so that policyholders and/or workshops can obtain more
compensation from insurers. The insurer should also identify fraud risk
factors in product design during the early stages of product development.
3.1.3 The insurer should establish appropriate indicators that when
triggered, suggests a higher risk of fraud. In the event that one or more
indicators are triggered, the insurer should ascertain the facts to determine
whether a more in-depth investigation and follow up actions are warranted.
There should be adequate documentation of the verification actions taken.
The indicators should be reviewed regularly for their continued relevance and
effectiveness in detecting fraud.

4.2 Documentation:
The Policyholder is required to submit all relevant documentation and information related to the claim, including but not limited to incident reports, financial records, forensic investigation results, and correspondence with third parties. The documentation should provide a comprehensive overview of the incident, impact assessment, and recovery efforts. 8.3 Access Control and Authentication:
The Policyholder is required to implement robust access control measures, including multi-factor authentication, least privilege access, and regular review of user access rights. Access to sensitive data and systems should be restricted to authorized personnel only, and all access should be logged and monitored for suspicious activity.

8.5 Data Encryption and Protection:
The Policyholder is required to implement data encryption for sensitive data at rest and in transit. Additional data protection measures, such as data loss prevention (DLP) tools and regular data backups, should be in place to prevent unauthorized access and data breaches. The Policyholder should conduct regular vulnerability assessments to identify and address potential security gaps.

5.8 Legal Compliance:
The Policyholder must comply with all applicable laws, regulations, and industry standards related to cybersecurity and data protection. Non-compliance may affect coverage eligibility and result in denial of claims arising from regulatory violations. The Policyholder is encouraged to seek legal counsel to ensure compliance with evolving legal requirements.

8.3 Access Control and Authentication:
The Policyholder is required to implement robust access control measures, including multi-factor authentication, least privilege access, and regular review of user access rights. Access to sensitive data and systems should be restricted to authorized personnel only, and all access should be logged and monitored for suspicious activity.

10.3 Contractual Obligations:
The Policyholder must fulfill its contractual obligations related to cybersecurity and data protection, as specified in agreements with customers, partners, and service providers. This includes adhering to service level agreements, implementing specified security measures, and reporting Cyber Incidents that may impact contractual relationships. Failure to comply with contractual obligations may result in legal disputes, which are covered under Technology Errors and Omissions Liability.

8.6 Third-Party Risk Management:
The Policyholder must assess and manage risks associated with third-party vendors and service providers. This includes conducting due diligence, establishing security requirements in contracts, and monitoring compliance with security standards. The Policyholder should require third parties to report any Cyber Incidents that may impact the Policyholder’s systems or data.

8.5 Data Encryption and Protection:
The Policyholder is required to implement data encryption for sensitive data at rest and in transit. Additional data protection measures, such as data loss prevention (DLP) tools and regular data backups, should be in place to prevent unauthorized access and data breaches. The Policyholder should conduct regular vulnerability assessments to identify and address potential security gaps.

3.2 Intentional Acts:
Coverage is excluded for any fraudulent, dishonest, or criminal acts committed by the Policyholder or its employees. This includes acts intentionally committed to cause harm or obtain unauthorized benefit, as well as any collusion or conspiracy to commit such acts. The policy also excludes coverage for acts committed with reckless disregard for the consequences, where the Policyholder could have reasonably foreseen the potential for harm.

2.10 Telecommunications Fraud:
Coverage for Telecommunications Fraud applies to losses resulting from unauthorized use of the Policyholder’s telecommunications systems, such as PBX hacking or toll fraud. The policy covers the cost of unauthorized calls, system audits, and implementation of enhanced security measures to prevent future incidents.

8.3 Access Control and Authentication:
The Policyholder is required to implement robust access control measures, including multi-factor authentication, least privilege access, and regular review of user access rights. Access to sensitive data and systems should be restricted to authorized personnel only, and all access should be logged and monitored for suspicious activity.

8.6 Third-Party Risk Management:
The Policyholder must assess and manage risks associated with third-party vendors and service providers. This includes conducting due diligence, establishing security requirements in contracts, and monitoring compliance with security standards. The Policyholder should require third parties to report any Cyber Incidents that may impact the Policyholder’s systems or data.

1.6 Third-Party Claim:
A Third-Party Claim is any claim made by an external party against the Policyholder as a result of a Cyber Incident. This includes claims for damages, legal fees, and other costs associated with the incident. Third-party claims can arise from customers, partners, vendors, or regulatory bodies and may involve allegations of negligence, breach of contract, or failure to comply with data protection laws.

6.3 Notification:
All notices required under this policy must be in writing and delivered to the respective party's address as stated in this contract. Notices may be delivered by hand, courier, registered post, or electronic mail with confirmation of receipt. The Policyholder must promptly update contact information to ensure receipt of important communications.

5.1 Confidentiality:
The terms and conditions of this policy, including any endorsements and amendments, must be kept confidential by both parties. Disclosure of policy details to any third party is prohibited without the prior written consent of the other party, except as required by law or regulatory authority. Breach of confidentiality may result in termination of coverage and potential legal action.

4.2 Documentation:
The Policyholder is required to submit all relevant documentation and information related to the claim, including but not limited to incident reports, financial records, forensic investigation results, and correspondence with third parties. The documentation should provide a comprehensive overview of the incident, impact assessment, and recovery efforts. Failure to provide complete and accurate documentation may result in denial of the claim.

8.4 Incident Response Planning:
The Policyholder must develop and maintain an incident response plan that outlines procedures for identifying, responding to, and recovering from Cyber Incidents. The plan should include roles and responsibilities, communication protocols, and escalation procedures. Regular testing and updates of the incident response plan are essential to ensure its effectiveness.

9.2 Case Study 2: Data Breach of Customer Records
Following a sophisticated phishing attack, Tech Solutions Ltd. discovers a data breach involving the unauthorized access of customer records, including personally identifiable information (PII). The Policyholder immediately notifies affected individuals and offers credit monitoring services, as required by data protection regulations. SecureNet Insurance Pvt. Ltd. covers the costs of notification, credit monitoring, and public relations efforts to manage the reputational impact. The Policyholder also benefits from Regulatory Defense and Penalties coverage to navigate regulatory investigations and potential fines.

1.1 Cyber Incident:
A Cyber Incident is defined as any event or series of events, whether accidental, negligent, or intentional, that lead to unauthorized access, use, disclosure, modification, or destruction of the Policyholder’s computer systems or data. This includes, but is not limited to, incidents involving hacking, malware, ransomware, phishing, denial of service attacks, social engineering tactics, and insider threats. Cyber Incidents are further categorized into minor, moderate, and severe based on the impact and extent of damage.

performing those procedures that are necessary to determine whether fraud has occurred, the loss
or exposures associated with the fraud, who was involved in it and the fraud scheme (how it
happened).

3.3 Fraud Risk Assessment
The Fraud Risk Team has the primary responsibility of establishing and monitoring all aspects of
fraud risk assessment and prevention activities. The fraud risk assessment must identify potential
fraud risk areas and the perpetrators. The assessment must be commensurate with the business
size of the Organization. Fraud Risk Team must establish policies and procedures to:
- Identify and assess frauds
- Set up procedures to mitigate the identified fraud risks
- Implement preventive and detective measures through internal controls
- Liaising with law enforcement agencies

7.5 Social Engineering Fraud Endorsement:
This endorsement provides coverage for financial losses resulting from social engineering fraud, including phishing and pretexting attacks. Coverage includes reimbursement for funds transferred to cybercriminals as a result of fraudulent instructions and costs associated with implementing enhanced security measures to prevent future occurrences. The endorsement requires the Policyholder to implement specific controls, such as dual authorization for fund transfers, to qualify for coverage.

9.2 Case Study 2: Data Breach of Customer Records
Following a sophisticated phishing attack, Tech Solutions Ltd. discovers a data breach involving the unauthorized access of customer records, including personally identifiable information (PII). The Policyholder immediately notifies affected individuals and offers credit monitoring services, as required by data protection regulations. SecureNet Insurance Pvt. Ltd. covers the costs of notification, credit monitoring, and public relations efforts to manage the reputational impact. The Policyholder also benefits from Regulatory Defense and Penalties coverage to navigate regulatory investigations and potential fines.

10.1 Data Protection and Privacy Laws:
The Policyholder must comply with applicable data protection and privacy laws, such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the Personal Data Protection Bill (PDPB) in India. Compliance includes obtaining consent for data processing, implementing data subject rights, and reporting data breaches to relevant authorities within statutory timeframes. Non-compliance may result in regulatory fines and penalties, which are partially covered under the policy.

8.3 Access Control and Authentication:
The Policyholder is required to implement robust access control measures, including multi-factor authentication, least privilege access, and regular review of user access rights. Access to sensitive data and systems should be restricted to authorized personnel only, and all access should be logged and monitored for suspicious activity.

policy_evidence.text: This manual serves as a comprehensive guide for managing risks and ensuring compliance within SecureLife Insurance Ltd., a leading insurance provider in India. An integral part of excellence in customer service is to have a prompt and responsive
mechanism to address customer grievances. This section lays down various provisions,
systems and procedures to ensure prompt and fair redressal of customer grievance
through a well-defined structure.
Grievances may originate because of one of the following reasons:
a. Gap between the actual product or service offered and the understanding of the
customer about it. This may be due to incomplete information or misinformation
about the product/service.
b. Failure to deliver a product or service as per the expectations of the customer.
c. Perceived Misselling or unfair business practices

philosophies

The Grievance Redressal mechanism at SBI Life is based on the following basic
philosophies
a. Grievance redressal will always be a focus area of senior management.
b. All the grievances shall be treated fairly, objectively and transparently.
c. Grievances raised shall be handled and resolved swiftly within a reasonable time
and in accordance with the applicable regulations.
d. All the aspects related to the grievance shall be taken into consideration before
providing a comprehensive solution.
e. All employees shall be educated and trained regularly to handle grievances with
empathy and in good faith without any prejudices about the complainant.
f. The complainant shall be provided information about the escalation mechanism
and other avenues available for him to seek a redressal in case he is not satisfied
with the resolution provided.

Mediation shall be conducted by a neutral third party, with costs shared equally by both parties. If mediation fails to resolve the dispute, the parties may proceed to arbitration or litigation, as specified in the policy conditions.

4.0 Process Flow of Complaints Handling
5.0 System Support & Tools for Grievance Management
Grievance management is supported by integrated system / CRM tool called “Simple CRM”. The main
functionalities of the system are:-
Interactive call logging system for all touch points
All touch points can log a complaint and scan images of the complaint letter through the system.
The system generates a Complaint Reference No. which is communicated to the customer. The
complaint is then resolved by the respective Process Owners at the Home Office. The resolution
by the respective process owners is also communicated to the customer.
Seamless tracking of all complaints
Once all touch points log the complaints in the system, the complaint status can be tracked by
various stakeholders at any given point of time.

GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL PROCEDURE
Annexure 2 of Policy on Protection of Policyholders’ interest
Grievance Redressal Procedure
Objective
An integral part of excellence in customer service is to have a prompt and responsive
mechanism to address customer grievances. This section lays down various provisions,
systems and procedures to ensure prompt and fair redressal of customer grievance
through a well-defined structure.
Grievances may originate because of one of the following reasons:
a. Gap between the actual product or service offered and the understanding of the
customer about it. This may be due to incomplete information or misinformation
about the product/service.
b. Failure to deliver a product or service as per the expectations of the customer.
c. Perceived Misselling or unfair business practices
The Grievance Redressal mechanism at SBI Life is based on the following basic
philosophies
a. Grievance redressal will always be a focus area of senior management.

The Grievance Redressal mechanism at SBI Life is based on the following basic
philosophies
a. Grievance redressal will always be a focus area of senior management.
b. All the grievances shall be treated fairly, objectively and transparently.
c. Grievances raised shall be handled and resolved swiftly within a reasonable time
and in accordance with the applicable regulations.
d. All the aspects related to the grievance shall be taken into consideration before
providing a comprehensive solution.
e. All employees shall be educated and trained regularly to handle grievances with
empathy and in good faith without any prejudices about the complainant.
f. The complainant shall be provided information about the escalation mechanism
and other avenues available for him to seek a redressal in case he is not satisfied
with the resolution provided.

Claim Review Committee (CRC)
Whenever a claim decision is taken and communicated to the claimant, there may arise
some dissatisfaction due to various reasons such as non-settlement of claim, incorrect
amount of claim settled, delay in claim settlement etc.
In order to ensure fair and unbiased resolution to the grievances of the
policyholders/claimants regarding claim settlement, the company shall form a Claims
Review Committee.
Policyholder/Claimant can approach the Claims Review Committee for resolution of
his/her grievances related to claims.
Composition of CRC
Exhibiting the commitment of the Company to provide a fair resolution the claimants’ grievance
in a transparent manner, the Claims Review Committee shall be constituted. A Retired High Court
Judge shall be member of the committee.
The composition of CRC is as follows:
o Retired Judge - High Court
o President (Ops & IT)
o President & CFO
o Chief Operating Officer
o Appointed Actuary
o Chief Actuary & Chief Risk Officer

for review. The CRC may uphold or change the original decision after reviewing the claimant’s
representation based on the merits of each individual case after scrutiny of the documents,
evidences and information presented to it.

policy_evidence.text: The Company will notify the Reinsurer of its intention to contest, compromise, or litigate a claim involving a reinsured policy, or to rescind coverage by the Company under a reinsured policy. The Company shall then submit to the Reinsurer for review, copies of the insured’s death certificate or other reliable proof of death as agreed to by the Reinsurer, claimant’s statement and, upon the Reinsurer’s request, any other papers connected with the claim or rescission.

In the event that the Reinsurer agrees with the Company’s decision to contest, compromise or litigate a claim, or to rescind coverage by the Company under a reinsured policy, the Reinsurer agrees to reimburse the Company for any reasonable legal, investigative and like expenses that the Company may incur in seeking to contest, compromise or litigate a claim under such reinsured policy, or to rescind such reinsured policy. Such reimbursement shall be in the proportion that the Reinsurer’s net liability for such reinsured policy bears to the sum of the net liability of the Company and all reinsurers for such reinsured policy, as of the date of rescission where the Company decides to rescind such reinsured policy. The Reinsurer shall also pay its share of the claim itself, if applicable.

It is understood, however, that in the event of such insolvency, the rehabilitator, conservator, receiver, liquidator or statutory successor of the Company shall give written notice of the pendency of a claim against the Company on the policy reinsured within a reasonable time after such claim is filed in the insolvency proceedings, and that during the pendency of such claim, the Reinsurer may investigate such claims and interpose, at its own expense, in the proceedings where such claim is to be adjudicated, any defense or defenses which it may deem available to the Company or its liquidator, rehabilitator, receiver, conservator or statutory successor.

The Ceding Company shall maintain responsibility for claims handling, including assessment, negotiation, and settlement of claims. The Reinsurer reserves the right to be consulted on claims exceeding $500,000 or those involving complex coverage issues.

10.1 Data Protection and Privacy Laws:
The Policyholder must comply with applicable data protection and privacy laws, such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the Personal Data Protection Bill (PDPB) in India. Compliance includes obtaining consent for data processing, implementing data subject rights, and reporting data breaches to relevant authorities within statutory timeframes. Non-compliance may result in regulatory fines and penalties, which are partially covered under the policy.

4.2 Documentation:
The Policyholder is required to submit all relevant documentation and information related to the claim, including but not limited to incident reports, financial records, forensic investigation results, and correspondence with third parties. The documentation should provide a comprehensive overview of the incident, impact assessment, and recovery efforts. Failure to provide complete and accurate documentation may result in denial of the claim.

4.7 Claim Dispute Resolution:
In the event of a dispute regarding the coverage or settlement of a claim, the parties agree to engage in mediation as a preliminary step before pursuing formal legal action. The party to which the notice is sent will respond to the notification in writing within fifteen (15) days.

4.7 Claim Dispute Resolution:
In the event of a dispute regarding the coverage or settlement of a claim, the parties agree to engage in mediation as a preliminary step before pursuing formal legal action. Mediation shall be conducted by a neutral third party, with costs shared equally by both parties. If mediation fails to resolve the dispute, the parties may proceed to arbitration or litigation, as specified in the policy conditions.

4.2 Documentation:
The Policyholder is required to submit all relevant documentation and information related to the claim, including but not limited to incident reports, financial records, forensic investigation results, and correspondence with third parties. The documentation should provide a comprehensive overview of the incident, impact assessment, and recovery efforts. Failure to provide complete and accurate documentation may result in denial of the claim.

After consideration of the pertinent papers, the Reinsurer shall promptly inform the Company of its underwriting decision. If the underwriting decision is acceptable to the Company and the Company’s policy is subsequently placed in force in accordance with the Company’s placement rules, the Company shall advise the Reinsurer in the manner described in Exhibit F.

The Company will notify the Reinsurer of its intention to contest, compromise, or litigate a claim involving a reinsured policy, or to rescind coverage by the Company under a reinsured policy. The Company shall then submit to the Reinsurer for review, copies of the insured’s death certificate or other reliable proof of death as agreed to by the Reinsurer, claimant’s statement and, upon the Reinsurer’s request, any other papers connected with the claim or rescission.

policy_evidence.text: This manual serves as a comprehensive guide for managing risks and ensuring compliance within SecureLife Insurance Ltd., a leading insurance provider in India. Established in 2005, SecureLife is committed to delivering innovative insurance solutions while maintaining robust risk management and compliance frameworks. The manual outlines the policies, procedures, and frameworks necessary to align with IRDAI regulations and industry best practices. It is intended to be used by the Board of Directors, management, and employees to foster a culture of risk awareness and compliance. By implementing the guidelines in this manual, SecureLife aims to enhance its operational resilience, maintain regulatory compliance, and achieve its strategic objectives of increasing market share by 15% annually over the next five years. This document will be reviewed and updated annually to ensure it remains aligned with the evolving business environment and regulatory landscape.

10.6 Insurance Regulations and Disclosure Requirements:
SecureNet Insurance Pvt. Ltd. operates in compliance with applicable insurance regulations and disclosure requirements. The Policyholder must provide accurate and complete information during the underwriting process and promptly report any changes in risk exposure. Failure to disclose material information may result in denial of coverage or cancellation of the policy. SecureNet Insurance Pvt. Ltd. is committed to transparency and ethical conduct in all insurance transactions.

6.3 Notification:
All notices required under this policy must be in writing and delivered to the respective party's address as stated in this contract. Notices may be delivered by hand, courier, registered post, or electronic mail with confirmation of receipt. The Policyholder must promptly update contact information to ensure receipt of important communications.

Third-party intermediaries who assist in the solicitation or procurement of admitted insurance products include insurance brokers, insurance agents and general agents licensed by the Insurance Commission
(IC). A person (such as an individual, partnership or corporation) must file an application for an insurance broker or insurance agent in the IC and pay the corresponding application fees to be licensed.
An insurance broker must comply with the minimum paid-up capital of PHP 20 million for an insurance broker, or PHP 50 million for both an insurance and reinsurance broker. To be issued with
a license, a brokerage company must have a qualified and approved soliciting official.

additional_regulatory_context.text: CHINA | The CBIRC does not explicitly prohibit insurers from appointing offshore agents or accepting business from offshore brokers. However, it is a general rule that Chinese insurers must not appoint any individual or institution or that has not obtained the required qualification (applicable license or permit issued by CBIRC) to engage in insurance sales activities, and must not pay any commission or give any other benefit to any institution or individual that has not obtained the required qualification. Offshore agents and brokers are not eligible to obtain the required licenses issued by CBIRC. Therefore, it would not be legally viable for insurers in China to appoint offshore agents, or to pay any commission or give any other benefit to offshore brokers in exchange for the business brought by them.

For instance, the IC has adopted Market Conduct Guidelines for the guidance, compliance and implementation of all life insurers and their agents doing business in the Philippines. Non-compliant companies, officers or agents will be subject to discretionary sanctions provided under the Insurance Code and imposed by the IC. Moreover, under the principal-agent principle in Philippine law, a principal is liable to third parties for the acts of its agent. However, the written agreement between the insurer and its agents may provide that the agent will indemnify the principal in cases of liability to third parties due to the agent’s acts. Under Philippine law, an agent must act in accordance with the instructions of the principal and answer for damages that the principal may suffer due to the agent’s fraud, negligence, or non-performance.

policy_evidence.text: This manual serves as a comprehensive guide for managing risks and ensuring compliance within SecureLife Insurance Ltd., a leading insurance provider in India. Established in 2005, SecureLife is committed to delivering innovative insurance solutions while maintaining robust risk management and compliance frameworks. The manual outlines the policies, procedures, and frameworks necessary to align with IRDAI regulations and industry best practices. It is intended to be used by the Board of Directors, management, and employees to foster a culture of risk awareness and compliance. By implementing the guidelines in this manual, SecureLife aims to enhance its operational resilience, maintain regulatory compliance, and achieve its strategic objectives of increasing market share by 15% annually over the next five years. This document will be reviewed and updated annually to ensure it remains aligned with the evolving business environment and regulatory landscape.

By transferring risk to reinsurers, SecureLife can manage its risk exposure more effectively, enhance capital efficiency, and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements. The objectives of the reinsurance program include optimizing the company's risk-retention balance, maintaining financial stability, and supporting business growth. With a diverse portfolio of over 500,000 policies and a target to increase premium income by 20% annually, a well-structured reinsurance program enhances SecureLife's resilience to adverse events and contributes to long-term financial sustainability.

additional_regulatory_context.text: SINGAPORE | Insurance providers in the market include direct life insurers and financial advisers, that are able to directly sell their relevant insurance products without the need for intermediaries. Entities that arrange life products or provide advice concerning life products will need to hold a financial adviser’s license or, if eligible, be registered with the MAS as an exempt financial adviser under the FAA. Entities that arrange general and long-term accident and health policies will need to hold a direct insurer license (or reinsurer or captive insurer) under the IA. We are not aware of any general restrictions on appropriately licensed insurers selling the relevant insurance products virtually without any intermediaries. policy_evidence.text: This manual serves as a comprehensive guide for managing risks and ensuring compliance within SecureLife Insurance Ltd., a leading insurance provider in India. Established in 2005, SecureLife is committed to delivering innovative insurance solutions while maintaining robust risk management and compliance frameworks. The manual outlines the policies, procedures, and frameworks necessary to align with IRDAI regulations and industry best practices. It is intended to be used by the Board of Directors, management, and employees to foster a culture of risk awareness and compliance. By implementing the guidelines in this manual, SecureLife aims to enhance its operational resilience, maintain regulatory compliance, and achieve its strategic objectives of increasing market share by 15% annually over the next five years. This document will be reviewed and updated annually to ensure it remains aligned with the evolving business environment and regulatory landscape.

additional_regulatory_context.text:
Asia Pacific Guide for Insurance Sales, Advisory and Distribution 2023 | 36
12 Tele and online channels
Are there specific requirements on selling products through online channels? (cont’d)
Where a direct life insurer or financial adviser provides direct purchase insurance products online without financial advice, they should bear in mind the safeguards set out under the ID 01/17
Guidelines on the Online Distribution of Life Policies with No Advice and/or FAA G-15 Guidelines on the Online Distribution of Life Policies with No Advice respectively that includes, the following,
among others:
a) Ensuring all equivalent direct purchase insurance products are available online if the life insurer or financial adviser offers a specific life policy online
b) Having in place the safeguards including the following:
i. Providing the client with prescribed information before the client completes the purchase of a life policy and obtaining client’s acknowledgement

additional_regulatory_context.text:
CHINA | As a general principle, insurers should enter into written agency agreements with their appointed agents that should stipulate the parties’ respective rights and obligations. There is no specific requirement on the exact form that these agreements should take.
HONG KONG | There is no prescribed or mandatory format on distribution agreements under law.
INDONESIA | Yes. There should be written agreements between the insurers and their appointed agents. Agreements must include, at a minimum, (1) in-agency agreements on ethical principles set by the association in accordance with the business lines; (2) obligations on the insurance agents to comply with the ethical code set by the association, together with applicable sanctions for every violation by the insurance agents; and (3) time periods for the submission of premiums and contributions to the insurers. Agreements should be in the Indonesian language.
JAPAN | No. There are no specific rules in this regard.

additional_regulatory_context.source_file: Guide for Insurance Sales Advisory and DIstribution.pdf
additional_regulatory_context.text:
Agreements with GIA-registered insurance agents should follow the form of the written agency agreement prescribed by the GIA (although customization is permitted). Other than this,
there is generally no specific requirement with respect to the forms of agreement between insurers and intermediaries, beyond that insurance agents must enter into a written agreement
SINGAPORE with their insurer that authorizes the insurance agent to arrange the relevant contract or class of contracts of insurance. In practice, terms relating to the appointment of any distributors or agents,
remuneration, ownership of and rights to client information, and allocation of liabilities and indemnities arising from any mis-selling or other misconduct should be set out clearly in the agreement.

It is intended to be used by the Board of Directors, management, and employees to foster a culture of risk awareness and compliance. By implementing the guidelines in this manual, SecureLife aims to enhance its operational resilience, maintain regulatory compliance, and achieve its strategic objectives of increasing market share by 15% annually over the next five years. policy_evidence.text: This manual serves as a comprehensive guide for managing risks and ensuring compliance within SecureLife Insurance Ltd., a leading insurance provider in India. Established in 2005, SecureLife is committed to delivering innovative insurance solutions while maintaining robust risk management and compliance frameworks. The manual outlines the policies, procedures, and frameworks necessary to align with IRDAI regulations and industry best practices. It is intended to be used by the Board of Directors, management, and employees to foster a culture of risk awareness and compliance. By implementing the guidelines in this manual, SecureLife aims to enhance its operational resilience, maintain regulatory compliance, and achieve its strategic objectives of increasing market share by 15% annually over the next five years. This document will be reviewed and updated annually to ensure it remains aligned with the evolving business environment and regulatory landscape.

additional_regulatory_context.text: PHILIPPINES | The IC has guidelines for selling life and non-life insurance products that insurers must follow. For instance, the IC has adopted Market Conduct Guidelines for the guidance, compliance and implementation of all life insurers and their agents doing business in the Philippines. Non-compliant companies, officers or agents will be subject to discretionary sanctions provided under the Insurance Code and imposed by the IC. Moreover, under the principal-agent principle in Philippine law, a principal is liable to third parties for the acts of its agent. However, the written agreement between the insurer and its agents may provide that the agent will indemnify the principal in cases of liability to third parties due to the agent’s acts. Under Philippine law, an agent must act in accordance with the instructions of the principal and answer for damages that the principal may suffer due to the agent’s fraud, negligence, or non-performance.

policy_evidence.text: This manual serves as a comprehensive guide for managing risks and ensuring compliance within SecureLife Insurance Ltd., a leading insurance provider in India. Established in 2005, SecureLife is committed to delivering innovative insurance solutions while maintaining robust risk management and compliance frameworks. The manual outlines the policies, procedures, and frameworks necessary to align with IRDAI regulations and industry best practices. It is intended to be used by the Board of Directors, management, and employees to foster a culture of risk awareness and compliance. By implementing the guidelines in this manual, SecureLife aims to enhance its operational resilience, maintain regulatory compliance, and achieve its strategic objectives of increasing market share by 15% annually over the next five years. This document will be reviewed and updated annually to ensure it remains aligned with the evolving business environment and regulatory landscape.

Under IC Circular Letter No. 2016-61, insurance companies and their brokers/agents are allowed to introduce, present and sell insurance products via telemarketing subject to the guidelines

and presentation of insurance products. Telemarketers engaged by insurance brokers will only be allowed to conduct a preliminary introduction and presentation of insurance products.

Asia Pacific Guide for Insurance Sales, Advisory and Distribution 2023 | 31
11 Tele and online channels
Are there specific requirements on selling products through call centers, telemarketing or other distribution channels? (cont’d)
Under IC Circular Letter No. 2016-61, insurance companies and their brokers/agents are allowed to introduce, present and sell insurance products via telemarketing subject to the guidelines
and requirements of the IC. Telemarketers engaged by insurance companies may or may not be IC-licensed insurance agents. A telemarketer that is an IC-licensed agent may solicit and/or sell
insurance product/s and receive appropriate commission for the sale. On the other hand, a telemarketer that is not an IC-licensed insurance agent is only allowed to conduct a preliminary introduction
and presentation of insurance products. Telemarketers engaged by insurance brokers will only be allowed to conduct a preliminary introduction and presentation of insurance products.

8.3 Access Control and Authentication:
The Policyholder is required to implement robust access control measures, including multi-factor authentication, least privilege access, and regular review of user access rights. Access to sensitive data and systems should be restricted to authorized personnel only, and all access should be logged and monitored for suspicious activity.

8.5 Data Encryption and Protection:
The Policyholder is required to implement data encryption for sensitive data at rest and in transit. Additional data protection measures, such as data loss prevention (DLP) tools and regular data backups, should be in place to prevent unauthorized access and data breaches. The Policyholder should conduct regular vulnerability assessments to identify and address potential security gaps.

5.6 Risk Mitigation:
The Policyholder agrees to implement and maintain appropriate cybersecurity measures and controls to mitigate the risk of Cyber Incidents. This includes, but is not limited to, regular system updates, employee training, and incident response planning. Failure to maintain adequate security measures may affect coverage eligibility. SecureNet Insurance Pvt. Ltd. may provide recommendations for risk mitigation practices, and compliance with these recommendations may be a condition of coverage.

8.7 Regular Security Audits:
The Policyholder is encouraged to conduct regular security audits and penetration testing to identify vulnerabilities and assess the effectiveness of security controls. Audits should be performed by qualified cybersecurity professionals and include recommendations for remediation. The Policyholder should address identified vulnerabilities in a timely manner and document corrective actions taken.

8.2 Employee Training:
The Policyholder must implement regular cybersecurity awareness training for all employees, contractors, and third-party partners. Training should cover topics such as phishing detection, password management, and safe browsing practices. The Policyholder should maintain records of training completion and update training materials to address emerging threats.

The Policyholder is required to implement data encryption for sensitive data at rest and in transit. 8.5 Data Encryption and Protection:
The Policyholder is required to implement data encryption for sensitive data at rest and in transit. Additional data protection measures, such as data loss prevention (DLP) tools and regular data backups, should be in place to prevent unauthorized access and data breaches. The Policyholder should conduct regular vulnerability assessments to identify and address potential security gaps.

5.6 Risk Mitigation:
The Policyholder agrees to implement and maintain appropriate cybersecurity measures and controls to mitigate the risk of Cyber Incidents. This includes, but is not limited to, regular system updates, employee training, and incident response planning. Failure to maintain adequate security measures may affect coverage eligibility. SecureNet Insurance Pvt. Ltd. may provide recommendations for risk mitigation practices, and compliance with these recommendations may be a condition of coverage.

8.1 Cybersecurity Framework:
The Policyholder is encouraged to adopt a recognized cybersecurity framework, such as the NIST Cybersecurity Framework or ISO/IEC 27001, to guide risk management practices. The framework should address key areas such as risk assessment, access control, incident response, and continuous monitoring. Compliance with the chosen framework may be a condition of coverage.

8.3 Access Control and Authentication:
The Policyholder is required to implement robust access control measures, including multi-factor authentication, least privilege access, and regular review of user access rights. Access to sensitive data and systems should be restricted to authorized personnel only, and all access should be logged and monitored for suspicious activity.

5.8 Legal Compliance:
The Policyholder must comply with all applicable laws, regulations, and industry standards related to cybersecurity and data protection. Non-compliance may affect coverage eligibility and result in denial of claims arising from regulatory violations. The Policyholder is encouraged to seek legal counsel to ensure compliance with evolving legal requirements.

4.2 Documentation:
The Policyholder is required to submit all relevant documentation and information related to the claim, including but not limited to incident reports, financial records, forensic investigation results, and correspondence with third parties. The documentation should provide a comprehensive overview of the incident, impact assessment, and recovery efforts. Failure to provide complete and accurate documentation may result in denial of the claim.

4.3 Cooperation:
The Policyholder must fully cooperate with SecureNet Insurance Pvt. Ltd. in the investigation and defense of any claim. This includes providing access to systems, records, and personnel as necessary to assess the extent of the Cyber Incident and determine coverage eligibility. Cooperation also involves participating in interviews, providing sworn statements, and assisting in the recovery of losses through subrogation efforts.

4.1 Notice of Claim:
The Policyholder must provide written notice to SecureNet Insurance Pvt. Ltd. within 48 hours of discovering a Cyber Incident that may give rise to a claim under this policy. The notice should include a description of the incident, date and time of occurrence, and any immediate actions taken to mitigate the impact. The Policyholder should utilize the designated claims portal or contact the claims hotline for prompt assistance.

policy_evidence.text: Improve Claims Assessment Accuracy: Integrate forensic cybersecurity investigations into claims assessment processes to improve accuracy and ensure fair settlements.

4.5 Subrogation Rights:
Upon payment of a claim, SecureNet Insurance Pvt. Ltd. is subrogated to all rights of the Policyholder to recover from any third party responsible for the loss. The Policyholder agrees to execute any documents and take any actions necessary to secure these rights. Subrogation efforts may include pursuing recovery from vendors, service providers, or other parties whose actions contributed to the Cyber Incident.

8.5 Data Encryption and Protection:
The Policyholder is required to implement data encryption for sensitive data at rest and in transit. Additional data protection measures, such as data loss prevention (DLP) tools and regular data backups, should be in place to prevent unauthorized access and data breaches. The Policyholder should conduct regular vulnerability assessments to identify and address potential security gaps.

8.3 Access Control and Authentication:
The Policyholder is required to implement robust access control measures, including multi-factor authentication, least privilege access, and regular review of user access rights. Access to sensitive data and systems should be restricted to authorized personnel only, and all access should be logged and monitored for suspicious activity.

The Policyholder must maintain a business continuity and disaster recovery plan to ensure the resumption of critical business operations in the event of a Cyber Incident. The plan should include contingency measures, such as alternative communication channels and backup systems, and be regularly tested and updated. The Policyholder should conduct post-incident reviews to evaluate the effectiveness of the plan and identify areas for improvement.

Tech Solutions Ltd. experiences a denial of service attack that disrupts its e-commerce platform, resulting in significant loss of online sales. The Policyholder activates its incident response plan and collaborates with internet service providers to mitigate the attack. SecureNet Insurance Pvt. Ltd. provides Business Interruption coverage to compensate for lost income and additional expenses incurred during the recovery process. The Policyholder conducts a post-incident analysis to strengthen its defenses against future denial of service attacks.

A Third-Party Claim is any claim made by an external party against the Policyholder as a result of a Cyber Incident. This includes claims for damages, legal fees, and other costs associated with the incident. Third-party claims can arise from customers, partners, vendors, or regulatory bodies and may involve allegations of negligence, breach of contract, or failure to comply with data protection laws.

10.2 Cybersecurity Regulations:
Tech Solutions Ltd. is required to adhere to industry-specific cybersecurity regulations, such as those applicable to financial services, healthcare, or critical infrastructure sectors. Compliance involves implementing baseline security controls, conducting regular risk assessments, and reporting significant Cyber Incidents to regulatory bodies. The Policyholder should maintain documentation of compliance efforts and be prepared for regulatory audits.

5.6 Risk Mitigation:
The Policyholder agrees to implement and maintain appropriate cybersecurity measures and controls to mitigate the risk of Cyber Incidents. This includes, but is not limited to, regular system updates, employee training, and incident response planning. Failure to maintain adequate security measures may affect coverage eligibility. SecureNet Insurance Pvt. Ltd. may provide recommendations for risk mitigation practices, and compliance with these recommendations may be a condition of coverage.

8.1 Cybersecurity Framework:
The Policyholder is encouraged to adopt a recognized cybersecurity framework, such as the NIST Cybersecurity Framework or ISO/IEC 27001, to guide risk management practices. The framework should address key areas such as risk assessment, access control, incident response, and continuous monitoring. Compliance with the chosen framework may be a condition of coverage.

The manual outlines the policies, procedures, and frameworks necessary to align with IRDAI regulations and industry best practices. It is intended to be used by the Board of Directors, management, and employees to foster a culture of risk awareness and compliance. By implementing the guidelines in this manual, SecureLife aims to enhance its operational resilience, maintain regulatory compliance, and achieve its strategic objectives of increasing market share by 15% annually over the next five years. This document will be reviewed and updated annually to ensure it remains aligned with the evolving business environment and regulatory landscape.

policy_evidence.text: This manual serves as a comprehensive guide for managing risks and ensuring compliance within SecureLife Insurance Ltd., a leading insurance provider in India. Established in 2005, SecureLife is committed to delivering innovative insurance solutions while maintaining robust risk management and compliance frameworks. The manual outlines the policies, procedures, and frameworks necessary to align with IRDAI regulations and industry best practices. 10.1 Data Protection and Privacy Laws:
The Policyholder must comply with applicable data protection and privacy laws, such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the Personal Data Protection Bill (PDPB) in India. Compliance includes obtaining consent for data processing, implementing data subject rights, and reporting data breaches to relevant authorities within statutory timeframes. Non-compliance may result in regulatory fines and penalties, which are partially covered under the policy.

10.5 Cross-Border Data Transfers:
The Policyholder must comply with legal requirements for cross-border data transfers, including obtaining necessary approvals and implementing data transfer agreements. Compliance with international data protection standards is essential to avoid legal challenges and ensure the protection of personal data. The Policyholder should seek guidance from legal experts to navigate complex data transfer regulations and mitigate associated risks.

4.2 Documentation:
The Policyholder is required to submit all relevant documentation and information related to the claim, including but not limited to incident reports, financial records, forensic investigation results, and correspondence with third parties. The documentation should provide a comprehensive overview of the incident, impact assessment, and recovery efforts. Failure to provide complete and accurate documentation may result in denial of the claim.

8.5 Data Encryption and Protection:
The Policyholder is required to implement data encryption for sensitive data at rest and in transit. Additional data protection measures, such as data loss prevention (DLP) tools and regular data backups, should be in place to prevent unauthorized access and data breaches. The Policyholder should conduct regular vulnerability assessments to identify and address potential security gaps.

5.8 Legal Compliance:
The Policyholder must comply with all applicable laws, regulations, and industry standards related to cybersecurity and data protection. Non-compliance may affect coverage eligibility and result in denial of claims arising from regulatory violations. The Policyholder is encouraged to seek legal counsel to ensure compliance with evolving legal requirements.

15 Data privacy and confidentiality
Can insurers share client information with insurance agents and brokers and vice versa? What data privacy or confidentiality laws apply? (cont’d)
Insurers can share information with insurance agents/brokers and vice versa, with the consent of customers.

The Policyholder should conduct regular vulnerability assessments to identify and address potential security gaps.

5.14 Identity and Access Management
Identity management and access control arrangements shall be established to provide
effective and consistent user administration by establishing identity accountability and
authentication to allow business applications/systems/ networks/computing devices
access to only authorized 'users'.

a) Access control mechanisms should:
I. Limit access in line with access policies set by owners of business applications and
systems.
II. Restrict the business application/system/ network/computing device capabilities that can
be accessed (e.g. by providing menus /groups that enable access only to the particular
capabilities needed to fulfill a defined role)
III. Supplement passwords (e.g. by using strong authentication such as smartcards,
biometrics or tokens), if and when necessary.

i) Generic User-Ids/Service IDs shall be avoided and where no alternative exists, it
shall be controlled, authorized by Business/Asset Owner, to avoid misuse to
compromise user accountability.
ii) Privilege generic user-IDs shall allow the user to only perform the intended activities
for which the user-IDs was created. Such IDs shall be authorized by business/Asset
owners
d) Remote Access-
i) Remote access to the Organization’s infrastructure shall be highly restricted and
controlled to prevent unauthorized access to the Organization’s infrastructure from
untrusted networks
ii) 'Users' seeking to gain privileged access to the Organization’s IT facilities via public or
other external networks shall do so via two factor authentications.

management process covering associated Risks, Change authorization, Business Continuity

2.1 Network Security Liability:
This coverage provides protection against legal liability arising from a Third-Party Claim due to a Cyber Incident affecting the Policyholder’s computer systems. Covered incidents include unauthorized access, transmission of malicious code, and denial of service attacks. Legal defense costs, settlement amounts, and damages awarded to third parties are included in the coverage. The policy also extends coverage to liabilities arising from failure to prevent unauthorized access to third-party systems through the Policyholder's network.

9.3 Case Study 3: Denial of Service Attack on E-Commerce Platform
Tech Solutions Ltd. experiences a denial of service attack that disrupts its e-commerce platform, resulting in significant loss of online sales. The Policyholder activates its incident response plan and collaborates with internet service providers to mitigate the attack. SecureNet Insurance Pvt. Ltd. provides Business Interruption coverage to compensate for lost income and additional expenses incurred during the recovery process. The Policyholder conducts a post-incident analysis to strengthen its defenses against future denial of service attacks.

9.4 Hypothetical Scenario: Insider Threat Leading to Data Theft
An employee of Tech Solutions Ltd. uses privileged access to steal sensitive intellectual property and sell it to a competitor. The Policyholder detects the unauthorized data transfer through its monitoring systems and takes immediate action to terminate the employee’s access and initiate legal proceedings. SecureNet Insurance Pvt. Ltd. covers the costs of forensic investigation and legal representation under the Network Security Liability and Technology Errors and Omissions Liability coverages. The Policyholder also enhances its access control measures and employee training programs to mitigate the risk of future insider threats.

Phishing is a social engineering attack where attackers impersonate legitimate entities to trick individuals into providing sensitive information such as login credentials or financial data. Phishing can occur via email, phone, or other communication channels. The policy covers losses arising from successful phishing attacks that lead to unauthorized access or data breaches.

An employee of Tech Solutions Ltd. uses privileged access to steal sensitive intellectual property and sell it to a competitor. The Policyholder detects the unauthorized data transfer through its monitoring systems and takes immediate action to terminate the employee’s access and initiate legal proceedings. SecureNet Insurance Pvt. Ltd. covers the costs of forensic investigation and legal representation under the Network Security Liability and Technology Errors and Omissions Liability coverages. 8.8 Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery:

The Policyholder should seek guidance from legal experts to navigate complex data transfer regulations and mitigate associated risks.

In the event of a dispute regarding the coverage or settlement of a claim, the parties agree to engage in mediation as a preliminary step before pursuing formal legal action. Mediation shall be conducted by a neutral third party, with costs shared equally by both parties. If mediation fails to resolve the dispute, the parties may proceed to arbitration or litigation, as specified in the policy conditions.

9.4 Hypothetical Scenario: Insider Threat Leading to Data Theft
An employee of Tech Solutions Ltd. uses privileged access to steal sensitive intellectual property and sell it to a competitor. The Policyholder detects the unauthorized data transfer through its monitoring systems and takes immediate action to terminate the employee’s access and initiate legal proceedings. SecureNet Insurance Pvt. Ltd. covers the costs of forensic investigation and legal representation under the Network Security Liability and Technology Errors and Omissions Liability coverages. The Policyholder also enhances its access control measures and employee training programs to mitigate the risk of future insider threats.

8.5 Data Encryption and Protection:
The Policyholder is required to implement data encryption for sensitive data at rest and in transit. Additional data protection measures, such as data loss prevention (DLP) tools and regular data backups, should be in place to prevent unauthorized access and data breaches. The Policyholder should conduct regular vulnerability assessments to identify and address potential security gaps.

9.2 Case Study 2: Data Breach of Customer Records
Following a sophisticated phishing attack, Tech Solutions Ltd. discovers a data breach involving the unauthorized access of customer records, including personally identifiable information (PII). The plan should include contingency measures, such as alternative communication channels and backup systems, and be regularly tested and updated. The Policyholder should conduct post-incident reviews to evaluate the effectiveness of the plan and identify areas for improvement.

2.3 Business Interruption:
Coverage for Business Interruption includes loss of income and additional expenses incurred due to a Cyber Incident that disrupts normal business operations. This coverage is subject to a waiting period of 12 hours, after which the loss of income will be calculated based on the Policyholder’s historical financial records. Additional expenses may include costs incurred to expedite the restoration of business operations, such as hiring temporary staff or leasing replacement equipment. The policy also provides coverage for contingent business interruption, which applies when a Cyber Incident affects a critical supplier or service provider.

8.6 Third-Party Risk Management:
The Policyholder must assess and manage risks associated with third-party vendors and service providers. This includes conducting due diligence, establishing security requirements in contracts, and monitoring compliance with security standards. The Policyholder should require third parties to report any Cyber Incidents that may impact the Policyholder’s systems or data.

6.6 Force Majeure:
Neither party shall be liable for any failure or delay in performance under this policy due to causes beyond their reasonable control, including acts of God, natural disasters, acts of war or terrorism, civil disturbances, and government actions. In the event of a force majeure, the affected party shall promptly notify the other party and make reasonable efforts to resume performance as soon as practicable.

3.6 Contractual Liabilities:
This policy excludes coverage for liabilities assumed by the Policyholder under any contract or agreement, unless such liability would have existed in the absence of the contract or agreement. The exclusion applies to indemnity clauses, warranties, and service level agreements that extend beyond the Policyholder’s standard business operations.

8.8 Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery:
The Policyholder must maintain a business continuity and disaster recovery plan to ensure the resumption of critical business operations in the event of a Cyber Incident. The plan should include contingency measures, such as alternative communication channels and backup systems, and be regularly tested and updated. The Policyholder should conduct post-incident reviews to evaluate the effectiveness of the plan and identify areas for improvement.

8.4 Incident Response Planning:
The Policyholder must develop and maintain an incident response plan that outlines procedures for identifying, responding to, and recovering from Cyber Incidents. The plan should include roles and responsibilities, communication protocols, and escalation procedures. Regular testing and updates of the incident response plan are essential to ensure its effectiveness.

5.6 Risk Mitigation:
The Policyholder agrees to implement and maintain appropriate cybersecurity measures and controls to mitigate the risk of Cyber Incidents. This includes, but is not limited to, regular system updates, employee training, and incident response planning. Failure to maintain adequate security measures may affect coverage eligibility. SecureNet Insurance Pvt. Ltd. may provide recommendations for risk mitigation practices, and compliance with these recommendations may be a condition of coverage.

6.6 Force Majeure:
Neither party shall be liable for any failure or delay in performance under this policy due to causes beyond their reasonable control, including acts of God, natural disasters, acts of war or terrorism, civil disturbances, and government actions. In the event of a force majeure, the affected party shall promptly notify the other party and make reasonable efforts to resume performance as soon as practicable.

2.6 Crisis Management and Public Relations:
In the event of a Cyber Incident, this coverage provides access to crisis management and public relations services to manage the impact on the Policyholder’s reputation. Services include media communication strategies, stakeholder engagement, and ongoing public relations support to rebuild trust with clients and partners. The policy also covers the costs of conducting customer satisfaction surveys and brand reputation analysis to assess the impact of the incident and guide recovery efforts.

1.2 Data Breach:
Data Breach refers to the unauthorized acquisition, access, use, or disclosure of confidential, sensitive, or personal data that compromises the security, confidentiality, or integrity of such data. This definition encompasses breaches involving electronic data as well as physical records, and includes data held by third-party service providers. The breach is considered significant if it involves personally identifiable information (PII), payment card information (PCI), or other sensitive data regulated under applicable data protection laws.

The breach is considered significant if it involves personally identifiable information (PII), payment card information (PCI), or other sensitive data regulated under applicable data protection laws.

The policy also covers the costs of conducting customer satisfaction surveys and brand reputation analysis to assess the impact of the incident and guide recovery efforts.

8.6 Third-Party Risk Management:
The Policyholder must assess and manage risks associated with third-party vendors and service providers. This includes conducting due diligence, establishing security requirements in contracts, and monitoring compliance with security standards. The Policyholder should require third parties to report any Cyber Incidents that may impact the Policyholder’s systems or data.

8.3 Access Control and Authentication:
The Policyholder is required to implement robust access control measures, including multi-factor authentication, least privilege access, and regular review of user access rights. Access to sensitive data and systems should be restricted to authorized personnel only, and all access should be logged and monitored for suspicious activity.

8.5 Data Encryption and Protection:
The Policyholder is required to implement data encryption for sensitive data at rest and in transit. Additional data protection measures, such as data loss prevention (DLP) tools and regular data backups, should be in place to prevent unauthorized access and data breaches. The Policyholder should conduct regular vulnerability assessments to identify and address potential security gaps.

8.1 Cybersecurity Framework:
The Policyholder is encouraged to adopt a recognized cybersecurity framework, such as the NIST Cybersecurity Framework or ISO/IEC 27001, to guide risk management practices. The framework should address key areas such as risk assessment, access control, incident response, and continuous monitoring. Compliance with the chosen framework may be a condition of coverage.

Additional expenses may include costs incurred to expedite the restoration of business operations, such as hiring temporary staff or leasing replacement equipment. The policy also provides coverage for contingent business interruption, which applies when a Cyber Incident affects a critical supplier or service provider.

2.6 Crisis Management and Public Relations:
In the event of a Cyber Incident, this coverage provides access to crisis management and public relations services to manage the impact on the Policyholder’s reputation. Services include media communication strategies, stakeholder engagement, and ongoing public relations support to rebuild trust with clients and partners. The policy also covers the costs of conducting customer satisfaction surveys and brand reputation analysis to assess the impact of the incident and guide recovery efforts.

The Policyholder should maintain documentation of compliance efforts and be prepared for regulatory audits.

16. Cryptography & Key Management

5.14 Identity and Access Management

8.8 Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery:
The Policyholder must maintain a business continuity and disaster recovery plan to ensure the resumption of critical business operations in the event of a Cyber Incident. The plan should include contingency measures, such as alternative communication channels and backup systems, and be regularly tested and updated. The Policyholder should conduct post-incident reviews to evaluate the effectiveness of the plan and identify areas for improvement.

8.3 Access Control and Authentication:

4.5 Subrogation Rights:
Upon payment of a claim, SecureNet Insurance Pvt. Ltd. is subrogated to all rights of the Policyholder to recover from any third party responsible for the loss. The Policyholder agrees to execute any documents and take any actions necessary to secure these rights. Subrogation efforts may include pursuing recovery from vendors, service providers, or other parties whose actions contributed to the Cyber Incident.

4.2 Documentation:
The Policyholder is required to submit all relevant documentation and information related to the claim, including but not limited to incident reports, financial records, forensic investigation results, and correspondence with third parties. The documentation should provide a comprehensive overview of the incident, impact assessment, and recovery efforts. Failure to provide complete and accurate documentation may result in denial of the claim.

8.4 Incident Response Planning:
The Policyholder must develop and maintain an incident response plan that outlines procedures for identifying, responding to, and recovering from Cyber Incidents. The plan should include roles and responsibilities, communication protocols, and escalation procedures. Regular testing and updates of the incident response plan are essential to ensure its effectiveness.

9.4 Hypothetical Scenario: Insider Threat Leading to Data Theft
An employee of Tech Solutions Ltd. uses privileged access to steal sensitive intellectual property and sell it to a competitor. The Policyholder detects the unauthorized data transfer through its monitoring systems and takes immediate action to terminate the employee’s access and initiate legal proceedings. SecureNet Insurance Pvt. Ltd. covers the costs of forensic investigation and legal representation under the Network Security Liability and Technology Errors and Omissions Liability coverages. The Policyholder also enhances its access control measures and employee training programs to mitigate the risk of future insider threats.

9.1 Case Study 1: Ransomware Attack on Financial Systems
In this scenario, Tech Solutions Ltd. experiences a ransomware attack that encrypts critical financial data, rendering accounting systems inoperable. The Policyholder quickly engages cybersecurity experts to contain the spread of the malware and begins negotiations with the attackers for decryption keys. SecureNet Insurance Pvt. Ltd. approves the payment of a ransom demand under the Cyber Extortion coverage, and the Policyholder successfully regains access to its data. The Policyholder also utilizes Business Interruption coverage to recover lost income during the downtime and implements enhanced security measures to prevent future incidents.

1.1 Cyber Incident:
A Cyber Incident is defined as any event or series of events, whether accidental, negligent, or intentional, that lead to unauthorized access, use, disclosure, modification, or destruction of the Policyholder’s computer systems or data. This includes, but is not limited to, incidents involving hacking, malware, ransomware, phishing, denial of service attacks, social engineering tactics, and insider threats. Cyber Incidents are further categorized into minor, moderate, and severe based on the impact and extent of damage.
